record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Random Matrix Theory and the Theory of Integrable Systems. II
record.original_question: Can one give a rigorous and explicit mathematical solution of the fixed-frequency diffraction problem for two slits in the plane, the classical double-slit problem underlying Young’s experiment and its quantum-mechanical analogues?

evidence.quote: However the rigorous solution of the problem of diffraction from two slits remains open.
This is a problem of the first order, whose rigorous and explicit solution would generate great interest in the mathematical and physics communities.

artifact.category_tag: Diffraction and Helmholtz boundary value problems
artifact.status_search_result: A rigorous and fully explicit closed-form solution to the fixed-frequency two-slit diffraction problem in the plane does not appear to be available. Boundary-integral and Wiener–Hopf approaches yield rigorous formulations and explicit solutions for a single slit/half-plane, and numerical or asymptotic treatments exist for multiple slits, but no explicit closed-form solution for two slits with arbitrary geometry and frequency has been established. The problem is widely regarded as still open.

status_evidence.title: A new explicit solution method for the diffraction through a slit
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit solution methods are developed for the single-slit Helmholtz diffraction problem via boundary operators with Hankel kernel.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous explicit treatments exist for single-slit diffraction; analogous explicit two-slit solutions are not reported.

status_evidence.snippet: Kirchhoff and Fresnel approaches to diffraction rely on approximations rather than exact rigorous solutions.
status_evidence.claim: Classical treatments of double-slit diffraction are approximate, not rigorous closed-form solutions.
